scenes.headline: How a lens reads a neuron from its weights
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Aperture! A lens turns one direction inside a model into a list of tokens. Here is how that works, and how well it holds up on a small model.

scenes.text: A lens linearises the layers above a neuron's write, so the weights alone predict which tokens steering the neuron will raise.
scenes.mark: predict which tokens steering the neuron will raise
scenes.say: A lens linearises the layers above a neuron's write. So the weights alone can predict which tokens steering that neuron will raise.

scenes.title: Reading a write through the layers above

steps.say: Take the neuron's write, one column of the down projection, and add it at every seed position.
Let the layers above act on it, and measure how the final residual changes.
Average that change, and read it through the unembedding to get a ranking of tokens.
Then compare the ranking with what steering the neuron really does.

parts.say: A softmax turns scores into a ranking of tokens.
The unembedding maps a vector to one score per token.

parts.note: The vector after the layers above
parts.say: J h is the vector after the layers above have acted on it.

scenes.title: Two ways to read a write

left.title: Logit lens
left.say: The logit lens skips the layers above, so it reads mostly noise in the early layers.

right.title: J-style read
right.say: The J-style read keeps them, by linearising, and it predicts steering from the first layers.

scenes.title: How well each read predicts steering at L8
scenes.say: At layer eight of this model, the J-style read correlates 0.80 with the measured steering effect. The logit lens gets 0.28, and another neuron's read gets 0.10.

scenes.label: of Qwen3-8B poles are dark to weight-only reads
scenes.say: But most mid-network neurons are dark to weight-only reads. The authors report 57 percent of poles fire, yet no token-level test explains them.

scenes.text: A weight-only read previews steering in the second half of the network, and is noisy in the first.
scenes.say: A weight-only read previews steering in the second half of the network, and it is noisy in the first.

recap: A lens reads a vector through the layers above
scenes.say: A lens reads a vector through the layers above it. The J-style read tracks steering, and the early layers are noisy.
